newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks firm at open on bid for TNT.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks firm at open on bid for TNT.

text.p: Australian shares opened firmer on Wednesday with the market bolstered by a surprise bid for transport group TNT which lifted the stock of other major transport companies and the whole market.

At 10.35 a.m. (0035 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 6.6 points higher at 2,292.1. The December share price index futures contract was up 13 points at 2,315 and at a 22.9 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said the TNT bid had given a positive balance to the market which otherwise was being held back by weak metal prices.
"The money out of the bid for TNT has to go somewhere," said Stuart Smith, senior dealer at Brisbane brokerage, Lance Jones.
Smith said transport group Mayne Nickless was now a strong target given that company's entitlements to the forthcoming float of telecommunications group, Optus.
"All thoughts of a possible rate cut seems to have evaporated and there appears to be some euphoria in the market about the record close of the Dow in the U.S.," Smith said.
Early turnover was healthy with Mayne Nickless the most active stock following the A$2 billion takeover offer for TNT by Dutch telecoms and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV.
